source_refs.note: Topic 9.18 with Figs. 9.31 and 9.32 (PDF 220-221, printed 217-218). Book errors are marked with Book correction boxes.

blocks.text: A potentiometer is mainly used to compare potential differences and to find the value of an unknown resistance. It works on the principle of Wheatstone Bridge.
book_errors: It works on the principle of Wheatstone Bridge.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: A potentiometer works on the principle that, with a steady current, the potential drop along a uniform wire is proportional to its length (V ∝ l), as the text below explains. What it shares with the Wheatstone bridge is the null method, not the principle.
